name: KamLAND2-Zen
summary: KamLAND2-Zen is the planned xenon-loaded scintillator programme using the KamLAND2 detector upgrade. Improved light collection and energy resolution are intended to distinguish a smaller neutrinoless signal from two-neutrino-decay backgrounds.
detection_principle: Enriched xenon in a scintillator balloon supplies the decay source. Higher light yield, upgraded photodetection and reduced backgrounds improve the calorimetric measurement around the xenon-136 endpoint.

status.label: Planned
status.evidence: The research profile distinguishes the completed original KamLAND observations from the detector upgrade; projected KamLAND2-Zen reach is a design goal.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
